Simon / Maria —

Great to meet you both. Short reply with our standard position and proposed next steps so procurement can proceed:

- Controller vs Processor: Redwood’s default is to be a processor; customers remain the controller. We are open to limited controller role in very narrow, customer-directed use cases but that requires explicit scoping in the DPA.
- SCC preference: for setups where the customer is the controller and Redwood acts as processor, we typically recommend the standard SCCs with an Annex that clarifies subprocessors and security measures (we can support Module 3 / controller-to-processor flow). If EU residency is required we can route to EU-dedicated capacity.
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently engaged in a SOC 2 Type II audit with a target report date of May 2028. We can provide an interim readiness letter and our most recent SOC 2 Type I evidence in advance.
- VSQ: please send the questionnaire and we'll aim to return an initial completed VSQ within 3 business days of receipt (track depends on depth).

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Responses_v1.pdf — initial mapping to your Aurelia template (redacted technical annexes).

Concrete next steps:
1) Maria to share VSQ and any redlines to the Aurelia DPA template (you already attached one).
2) Marcus will advise on SCC Annex language and any data residency clauses.
3) Redwood to provide SOC 2 readiness letter + subprocessor list link.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-min follow-up with procurement/legal next week to walk the DPA mapping.
